title: Duplicate new URLs in one sync batch can fail the whole request at commit time

evidence.quote: existing_feeds = {f.url: f for f in session.exec(existing_statement).all()}

reasoning: The handler snapshots existing URLs before processing and never updates that map after adding a new Feed. If the payload contains the same previously unknown URL twice, both entries take the create branch and are committed together. Since feed URLs are modeled as unique, this turns a client input issue into a commit-time database failure instead of a deterministic 4xx response or deduplicated update.
reproduction: POST /api/feeds/sync with two objects that have the same new URL but different titles. Both pass URL validation and both are added before session.commit(), causing the batch to fail rather than returning a stable sync result.
recommendation: Validate duplicate URLs within the incoming payload before mutating the session and return 422 with the duplicate URL, or update existing_feeds as new rows are staged so later entries are treated as updates under a documented last-write-wins policy.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current test uses two distinct URLs and only checks the synced count, so it does not exercise duplicate input or commit failure behavior.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a sync test that submits duplicate URLs in one payload and asserts the chosen contract: either 422 with a duplicate-url error or a successful deduplicated result with one stored feed.
minimumFixScope: Add per-request duplicate URL handling in sync_feeds and cover it in tests/test_feeds.py.
